exercises.prompt: Your friend says: «Também prefiro este café.» Say: «I agree with you.»
exercises.explanation: Use «concordar com» to agree with a person. With a friend, «contigo» makes the phrase natural.

exercises.prompt: Your friend says the metro is faster, and you think he is right. Say: «You're right.»
exercises.explanation: For informal singular, European Portuguese uses «tu» forms: «tens razão».

exercises.prompt: A friend asks if the film is good. You think so, but you are not 100% sure. Say: «I think so.»
exercises.explanation: «Acho que sim» is a soft way to say yes when you are fairly sure but not completely certain.

exercises.prompt: Two cafés are both fine for you. Say: «Either is fine.»
exercises.explanation: «Tanto faz» is a fixed chunk for when both options are okay. Learn it whole.

exercises.prompt: Your friend says sorry for being five minutes late. Reassure him: «It's okay.»
exercises.explanation: «Não faz mal» is a common set phrase to reassure someone after a small problem or mistake.

exercises.prompt: Your friend got the job. Say that you are happy for them.
exercises.explanation: Use «por ti» to react positively to good news from a friend. Learn the whole phrase as a chunk.

exercises.prompt: You said something silly and your friend looks shocked. Say: «I'm joking.»
exercises.explanation: European Portuguese uses «estar a + infinitive»: «estou a brincar». Learn the whole phrase as a set expression.

exercises.prompt: Your friend says: «Quero dizer que hoje não posso.» Ask him what he means.
exercises.explanation: To ask for clarification with a friend, use «O que queres dizer?». The version with «é que» is also common.
exercises.givenAnswer: Quero dizer que hoje não posso.
acceptedAnswers: O que é que queres dizer?

exercises.prompt: Your classmate says something confusing. Ask: «How do you mean?»
exercises.explanation: «Como assim?» is a short fixed question when something sounds confusing or surprising.
exercises.givenAnswer: Quero dizer que o autocarro já saiu.

exercises.prompt: You did not hear the last sentence. Ask your friend to repeat it.
exercises.explanation: «Podes repetir?» is the normal informal way to ask a friend to say it again.
exercises.givenAnswer: Disse que o café fecha às seis.

exercises.prompt: At reception, you do not understand well. Ask the receptionist (formal) to speak more slowly.
exercises.explanation: With strangers or staff, use the formal 3rd-person form: «Pode falar mais devagar?»
acceptedAnswers: Pode falar mais devagar, por favor?
O senhor pode falar mais devagar?
A senhora pode falar mais devagar?

exercises.prompt: Complete the mini-dialogue with two common conversation phrases.
exercises.explanation: «Não sei bem» shows uncertainty, while «Depende» means the answer changes with the situation.

exercises.prompt: Complete the reaction with the two fixed phrases.
exercises.explanation: «A sério?» reacts with surprise, and «Não acredito!» shows stronger surprise. Learn both as chunks.
exercises.template: — O Rui vai casar. — A ___? Não ___!

exercises.prompt: Fill the two gaps in this short exchange.
exercises.explanation: «Não faz mal» reassures someone after a small problem. «Ainda bem» shows relief after good news.
exercises.template: — Desculpa o atraso! — Não ___ mal. Encontraste as chaves? — Sim, encontrei. — ___ bem!

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: With informal singular «tu», the verb is «tens»: «Tens razão». «Tem» is the 3rd-person form.

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: To give your own opinion, use the first person: «não concordo». «Concordas» is the informal «you agree» form.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: Use «Depende.» when the answer changes from case to case. Learn it as a whole response.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: After «podes», the next verb stays in the infinitive: «repetir».

exercises.prompt: Answer about yourself.
exercises.explanation: Short fixed phrases are very common here. You can combine encouragement with reassurance.
exercises.question: O que costumas dizer a um amigo antes de um exame?
exercises.sampleAnswer: Costumo dizer: Força! Vai correr bem.

exercises.prompt: Good news from a friend. Put the dialogue in order.
exercises.explanation: A natural reaction often goes from surprise («A sério?») to joy («Que bom!») and then a warm comment.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sabes? Passei no exame de condução.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Que bom! Estou contente por ti.

exercises.prompt: Your friend says: «O concerto foi cancelado.» React with sympathy: «What a pity!»
exercises.explanation: Use «Que pena!» for disappointing news. Learn it as a whole reaction.

exercises.prompt: A classmate worries because he sent you the file a bit late. Reassure him casually: «No problem.»
exercises.explanation: «Sem problema.» is a short, casual way to say there is no problem. Use it as a fixed chunk.

exercises.prompt: Your friend says she got tickets for the festival. React enthusiastically, informally: «Cool!»
exercises.explanation: «Que fixe!» is an informal reaction to good news. It is common in European Portuguese.

exercises.prompt: Your flatmate suggests meeting at seven. Say: «Sounds good to me.»
exercises.explanation: Use «Parece-me bem.» to react positively to a suggestion. Learn the whole phrase as one chunk.

exercises.prompt: A friend says: «Em Lisboa há muito trânsito.» Agree with the short reaction «Yeah, that's true.»
exercises.explanation: «Pois é.» shows agreement or recognition. It often means “yes, that’s true”.

exercises.prompt: In a discussion about a film, you disagree, but softly. Say: «I don't really agree.»
exercises.explanation: «Não concordo muito.» softens disagreement. It sounds less direct than a strong «Não concordo.»

exercises.prompt: At the pharmacy, the assistant explains the medicine very fast. Ask her politely to say it again.
exercises.explanation: With strangers or staff, use the formal fixed phrase «Pode repetir?». It uses the 3rd-person form.

exercises.prompt: Your friend is speaking too fast. Ask him informally to slow down.
exercises.explanation: For a friend, use «podes». The full chunk is «Podes falar mais devagar?».

exercises.prompt: A shop assistant says something unclear about today’s opening hours. Ask politely what she means.
exercises.explanation: To ask for clarification formally, use «O que quer dizer?». A common alternative is with «é que».
exercises.givenAnswer: Quero dizer que hoje fechamos mais cedo.
acceptedAnswers: O que é que quer dizer?

exercises.prompt: An older neighbour tells you he finally sold his house. React politely and say you are happy for him.
exercises.explanation: Use «Fico contente por si.» in formal situations; «por ti» is only for friends. Learn it as a whole expression.

exercises.prompt: Complete the reaction to good news.
exercises.explanation: Use «Que bom!» for happy news and «Ainda bem.» when there is also relief. Both are fixed reactions.
exercises.template: — Passei no exame de condução. — ___ ___! ___ bem.

exercises.prompt: Complete the short dialogue about traffic.
exercises.explanation: «Acho que não.» is a soft negative answer. «Pois é.» shows agreement with the situation.
exercises.template: — Achas que eles chegam cedo? — ___ que ___. — ___ é, há muito trânsito.

exercises.prompt: Complete the opinion phrase.
exercises.explanation: «Na minha opinião…» introduces your personal view. Learn this opening as a chunk.
exercises.template: — Vamos já? — ___ ___ opinião, é melhor esperar.

exercises.prompt: Complete the answer when both options give the same result.
exercises.explanation: «Não faz diferença.» means the result is the same either way. It is a fixed phrase.
exercises.template: — Vamos de comboio ou de autocarro? — Não ___ ___.

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: With «a senhora», European Portuguese uses the 3rd-person form: «pode». «Podes» is informal singular.

exercises.prompt: One word is wrong. Tap it and choose the correction.
exercises.explanation: The phrase is «fico contente por si». After «contente», use «por» here, not «para».

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: For «I agree», the Portuguese form is «concordo». It is the «eu» form.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Portuguese for the word in bold.
exercises.explanation: In the reaction «Que alívio!», the noun is «alívio». Learn the whole phrase as a chunk.
exercises.sentence: What a **relief** — the train is on time!

exercises.prompt: Put the mini-dialogue in order.
exercises.explanation: «Boa sorte!» wishes someone luck. When they say they are nervous, «Força! Vai correr bem.» encourages and reassures them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Obrigado. Mas estou um bocadinho nervoso.

exercises.prompt: Answer about yourself.
exercises.explanation: Use «Isso mesmo.» to confirm that someone understood correctly. It is a fixed confirmation phrase.
exercises.question: O que dizes quando alguém dá a resposta certa?
